identification.full_name: U.S. Climate Reference Network (USCRN) Daily Products (Daily01)
identification.doi_note: This DOI belongs to NCEI's record for all the USCRN quality-controlled datasets (gov.noaa.ncdc:C00546), which includes the daily product; Daily01 has no DOI of its own. The DOI 10.1175/BAMS-D-12-00170.1 is a paper about the network (Diamond et al. 2013), not the dataset.
identification.data_provider: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI)
identification.description: Quality-controlled daily measurements from NOAA's nationwide U.S. Climate Reference Network, a network of stations built to give long-term, consistent climate observations for monitoring climate variability and change. NOAA NCEI archives and distributes the data; NOAA's Atmospheric Turbulence and Diffusion Division (ATDD) runs the stations.

curator.name: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI)

contributors: NOAA Atmospheric Turbulence and Diffusion Division (ATDD), Air Resources Laboratory
people.note: Howard Diamond is the named USCRN Program Manager. ATDD manages and maintains the stations; NCEI archives and curates the data.

instruments.summary: Automated weighing precipitation gauges, with a rain detector and a comparison tipping-bucket gauge.

categories.name: Geonor T-200B weighing precipitation gauge
categories.role: Primary instrument for the official precipitation values: three vibrating-wire load-cell sensors give independent depth readings every 5 minutes; wind/snow shield and heater

categories.name: Vaisala DRD11A rain detector
categories.role: Detects precipitation and its intensity, to tell real precipitation from other changes in gauge depth

categories.name: Hydrological Services TB-3 tipping-bucket rain gauge
categories.role: Auxiliary, for comparison at most stations; not quality-controlled and not used for the official values

instruments.note: The Geonor T-200B gives the official precipitation measurements; the rain detector and tipping-bucket gauge are supporting or comparison instruments.

temporal.start_note: Start of the USCRN observational record. Stations were installed at different dates, so each station's period of record differs.
temporal.input_frequency: 5-minute precipitation measurements, processed into daily values
temporal.note: Besides daily precipitation, the daily files include maximum, minimum and average air temperature, solar radiation, relative humidity, surface temperature, and soil moisture and temperature.

spatial.coverage: United States: contiguous U.S., Alaska and Hawaii
spatial.note: Stations are placed across representative climate regions. The extent is the catalog's broad bounding box, not a claim that observations fill it. Use the station coordinates for spatial analysis rather than a grid resolution.

data_format.format: Text files, one per station per year
